title: 31. Industry perspectives on professional standards and essential competencies for workforce preparedness.
content:
Abstract
Modern livestock marketing has evolved in response to digital innovation, changing industry demographics, and evolving industry expectations for engagement. The purpose of this descriptive qualitative study was to explore livestock marketing professionals’ perspectives on effective livestock marketing practices and implications for undergraduate curriculum development. The study was guided by the research question: How do livestock marketing professionals perceive successful marketing practices and what competencies are needed to prepare undergraduate students for careers in the livestock industry? After receiving Institutional Review Board (IRB) approval (#2024-217), semi-structured interviews were recorded and transcribed. Participants included livestock marketing professionals (n = 7) who were engaged with the Cal Poly Bull Test Program. Inductive thematic analysis was conducted using a systematic coding process in which two researchers independently reviewed transcripts and met to establish consensus on final themes. The resulting four themes were the following: (1) digital integration as essential to modern livestock marketing, (2) relationship-centered marketing as foundational to buyer loyalty, (3) brand identity and consistency as differentiators of successful programs, and (4) workforce competency development to meet industry expectations. Online sale platforms and strong digital presence were described as essential and no longer optional, increasing competition, broadening reach, and improving accessibility for producers facing geographic, labor, and time constraints. Successful marketing was characterized by an integrative approach combining digital and print media with personal communication. Relationship-centered marketing emphasized year-round engagement, customer service, and consistent pre- and post-sale communication grounded in trust and integrity, fostering repeat buyers and long-term viability. Clear production focus and consistent branding across digital and print platforms were identified as hallmarks of exemplary programs. Marketing materials that communicated industry commitment, authenticity, family values, and tradition further reinforced brand identity. For workforce preparation, participants emphasized interpersonal competencies such as resilience, time management, initiative, and professional relationship development alongside technical skills in production knowledge, business literacy, digital marketing, and graphic design. Findings suggest that animal science programs should intentionally integrate digital marketing strategy, brand development, business literacy, and relationship-centered communication into experiential livestock marketing curricula. However, these competencies demonstrate broad relevance across animal science disciplines.
